items.title: OpenAI Tries to Ease Backlash Against AI Data Centers
items.summary:
Broader rules and outside scrutiny would carry more weight than an individual company's promises, Perez-Etchegoyen said.

"OpenAI's own blueprint concedes that voluntary measures don't provide durable confidence. What would reduce uncertainty is the blueprint's proposals becoming law and applying to everyone who builds AI capacity, plus independent verification," he said. "Until then, enterprises should read this as a signal, not a planning assumption." [...] The company said it will disclose site-level water and electricity use, publish construction plans and commission independent noise studies before operations begin and then perform them annually afterward. The company says it will stop requiring nondisclosure agreements from public officials as a condition of negotiations, while retaining narrow protections for security and commercially sensitive information. [...] OpenAI said that the policy proposals build on work the company began in January when it announced its Stargate Community commitments to pay its own way on energy and develop plans shaped by local priorities.

"We followed with specific commitments in Georgia and Ohio, covering energy costs, water use, local investment and accountability," OpenAI wrote. "Today’s announcement is the next step in that ongoing effort."

items.title: Op-Ed: Tin hit by AI stock rout despite physical market tightness - Mining.com
items.summary: Micro Gold Futures $ 4073 / ozt  -0.61%. Micro Silver Futures $ 51.955 / ozt  0.25%. Gold Futures $ 4073.2 / ozt  -0.62%. Tin, which had been riding the AI wave on the back of its use as an electronic solder, has taken a particularly hard knock after Wall Street lost $3.2 trillion in a single session on Thursday as investors feared Democrats could slow the buildout of AI data centers. London Metal Exchange (LME) three-month tin CMSN3 has slumped from over $50,000 per metric ton to an eight-month low of $45,360 in the space of a week. The bursting of tin’s AI-investment bubble is ironically ill-timed since the market is the tightest it’s been in many months. The benchmark cash-to-three-months spread CMSN0-3 was in a deep contango, with prompt tin at a discount of more than $350 per ton to three-month delivery in August. Off-warrant inventory has also fallen to 1,089 tons, down 1,535 tons since the start of the year.

items.title: Cornish Metals raises $181m to fund South Crofty tin project in UK - Mining Technology
items.summary: # Cornish Metals raises $181m to fund South Crofty tin project in UK. Cornish Metals has completed a fundraising round, securing £135m ($181m) before expense through the issue of 225 million new ordinary shares to support the South Crofty tin project in Cornwall, UK. The fundraising structure involved a conditional placing of 33,977,873 shares, generating £20.4m, a conditional subscription for 181,002,661 shares that raised £108.6m and the conditional issuance of 10,019,466 shares under a retail offer, bringing in £6m. Cornish Metals focuses on mineral exploration and development in the UK, with its primary efforts centred on the wholly owned and permitted South Crofty tin project. Cornish Metals CEO Don Turvey said: “We are delighted to have completed this fundraise, which completes the financing package for the construction of South Crofty through to first tin in mid-2028. “I would like to thank our existing shareholders, Vision Blue and the National Wealth Fund, for their continued support, and to welcome our new investors, including our offtake partner Glencore and Leonidsport.

items.title: Cornish Metals faces costly financing hurdle - Mining.com
items.summary: Henry Lazenby | October 20, 2026 | 11:51 am  News Europe Tin. South Crofty tin project in the UK. Cornish Metals (AIM: TIN) is seeking £135 million ($180 million) through a deeply discounted share sale to unlock financing for its South Crofty tin mine’s restart, warning it could be unable to pay its debts if the deal fails. The equity sale would release $210 million of bond financing held in escrow, subject to other conditions. It puts a price on a funding problem that Cornish has disclosed for months: Shareholders face substantial dilution to advance the project, even with backing from Glencore (LSE: GLEN) and Britain’s National Wealth Fund. Glencore has conditionally agreed to invest £11.2 million and signed an agreement to buy all South Crofty’s tin concentrate for six years from commercial production. Cornish’s funding plan allocates £185 million to project capital spending, £55 million to converting existing shareholder loans and accrued interest into equity and £32 million to bond interest during construction and the production ramp-up.

items.title: Alphamin directs Congo tin to new US smelter - Mining.com
items.summary: Micro Gold Futures $ 4147.7 / ozt  1.79%. Gold Futures $ 4147.7 / ozt  1.80%. # Alphamin directs Congo tin to new US smelter. Henry Lazenby | November 9, 2026 | 2:28 pm  Base Metals News Africa United States Tin. Processing facilities at Alphamin Resources’ Bisie tin mine in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Alphamin Resources (TSXV: AFM; JSE: APH) has agreed to supply a new U.S. smelter with tin concentrate from the Democratic Republic of Congo, diversifying its sales as Washington backs domestic minerals processing. The material is destined for U.S. refiner Nathan Trotter & Co.’s $65-million (C$92 million) smelter in Virginia, which targets first production next year, Mauritius-based Alphamin said Monday. “Alphamin has been actively seeking to diversify its customer base and to support the development of western tin refining capacity,” the company said in a release. The allocation would account for up to 18% of Bisie’s targeted annual output, linking an established African mine to new U.S. processing capacity.
